# Modules that are INTENTIONALLY red, one Lake target per line.
#
# The breaker/builder discipline in AGENTS.md has a phase in which a frozen
# red battery exists and its implementation does not. During that phase the
# default build cannot be green, and a trust gate whose control step demands a
# green build cannot run at all.
#
# This file makes that phase explicit rather than letting the gate abort. It is
# self-checking in both directions: an undeclared failure fails the gate, and a
# declared module that is actually GREEN also fails the gate, so an entry
# cannot outlive the red phase it describes.
#
# Removing the last entry restores the original all-green control.
#
# ## The format
#
# A bare line is a Lean module. Two comment forms are structured, and they are
# comments precisely so that the two parsers that already read this file --
# `Test/Audit/AxiomGate.lean` (declaredRedModules) and
# `scripts/test-trust-gate.sh` -- keep reading exactly the module lines they
# read before, unchanged:
#
#   # reason: <text>   the named failure reason of every entry below it, until
#                      the next `# reason:` line. An entry with no reason in
#                      force is a defect and the policy refuses to load.
#   # gate: <name>     a sweep gate (scripts/sweep.sh's table) rather than a
#                      Lean module, for a gate that is red for a declared
#                      reason. The gate still runs; its owning script asks this
#                      file whether the failure was declared.
#
# `scripts/lib/known-red.sh` is the reader and the judge; per entry it reports
# `red as declared`, `UNEXPECTED PASS` or `not built`, and it refuses on an
# UNEXPECTED PASS or on any failure this file does not declare. Run
# `scripts/check-known-red.sh --list` to see the table and `--self-test` to
# exercise the policy without a build.
#
# History: the payload battery Test.Schema.PayloadContract was declared
# here during its red phase and removed when the builder turned it green; the
# gate itself caught the stale entry and refused to run until it was cleared.
#
# History: Test.Machine.Environment.ContextKeyContract, the frozen breaker
# battery for environment-slice node L0, fence F-KEY (src/Effect4/Machine/Key.lean),
# packet Test/contracts/environment-context-key.contract.md, was declared here
# during its red phase and removed when the builder turned it green.

# History: Test.Protocol.ByteParserContract (the W0 byte parser breaker) and
# Test.Concurrency.RaceRepresentativeContract (the binary race closure packet)
# were declared here from their birth; both lanes were retired on 2026-09-04 with
# their batteries deleted, so the list is empty and the all-green control holds.

# History: The Surface library's frozen breaker packet (26 modules) was retired
# on 2026-09-10 and archived to branch `archive/surface`.

# History: the gates `avatar-witnesses` and `armmap-citations` were declared here from
# 62c04d9 (the hand-written avatar predated the join, the scheduler and the timer) until
# 2026-09-08, when the avatar and the daemon were archived on `archive/ocaml5-avatar` and
# both gates were deleted with them.

# History: the gate `engine-tests` was declared here from the timer commit (e2285a9) until
# 2026-09-10, when the OCaml engine was regenerated at HEAD with the choose removal and
# `dune test engine` passed; the entry was removed deliberately on that unexpected pass.

# reason: the two flat LCNF outputs `ocaml/gen/fibers_gen.ml` and `machine_gen.ml` were cut before e2285a9; regenerating them at HEAD builds, but the hand-written `ocaml/gen/gen_check.ml` still tests the pre-timer machine shape (no Task_wake, no wake_list/clock_step/prepare_answer) and fails C2. Cleared when gen_check.ml is brought to the timer and external rows (DI-19's Phase 1)
# gate: generated-stale
